newsitem.title: USA: CVS to shed 120 Revco stores in FTC pact.
newsitem.headline: CVS to shed 120 Revco stores in FTC pact.

text.p: CVS Corp said Friday that it will sell 120 Revco D.S. Inc stores under an agreement with the U.S. Federal Trade Commission as part of the merger of the two drug store chains.
CVS said the FTC agreement has allowed it to complete the $2.8 billion merger with Revco, which also involves CVS assuming about $900 million of Revco debt.
To satisfy FTC concerns about the huge market presence the merger of the two retail drug industry giants, CVS agreed to give up 120 Revco stores in Virginia and New York state.
CVS said 114 Virginia stores are in the Richmond and Tidewater areas will be sold to Eckerd Corp, a division of J.C. Penney Co Inc.
The remaining stores, located in Binghamton, N.Y., will be sold to Medicine Shoppe International Inc.

Under the merger, each share of Revco being exchanged for 0.8842 CVS shares. About 60 million CVS shares will be issued to Revco shareholders, based on a total of about 67.8 million outstanding Revco shares, excluding about four million Revco stock options.

"We are very pleased to complete this merger, which brings together two industry leaders and will provide new opportunities for CVS to accelerate its growth," CVS chairman and chief executive officer Stanley Goldstein said in a statement.
